title: Terraform storage module: immutability guards, snapshot verification, encryption-first defaults
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Add immutability guards and an automated snapshot verification pipeline to the Terraform storage module (EBS, EFS, S3) with secure defaults for encryption, lifecycle policies, and cross-account snapshot handling. This ticket scopes the module changes, healthcheck hooks, and testing required to ship a backwards-compatible v2 release that prevents accidental data loss during upgrades and enforces encryption/KMS hygiene by default.

Scope of work (high level):
- Add optional immutable snapshot lifecycle for S3-backed exports and EBS snapshots (configurable retention + retention-override approval flow).
- Build Terraform module inputs for encryption-first defaults: CMK selection or auto-create with key rotation enabled, deny-unencrypted rule, and explicit KMS grants pattern for cross-account replication.
- Enforce EFS/TLS and mount target policies to avoid world-readable exports in VPC private deployments.
- Include S3 bucket hardened defaults (block public access, MFA-delete option, default lifecycle to move to infrequent/cold, object lock optional).
- Implement a snapshot verification job (Lambda/Step Function) triggered post-snapshot to validate snapshot integrity and replication status; expose status via CloudWatch metric and a small Terraform data source that can be polled during CI to gate upgrades.
- Add terraform-level healthcheck resources (local-exec / external data) that publish a simple health tuple (latest-snapshot-age, encryption-mode, last-verified-timestamp) to the monitoring stack.
- Migration and upgrade guidance: terraform state migration helpers, canary upgrade strategy, backward-compatible toggles and kill-switch for automated deletion policies.

Out of scope: full on-prem storage drivers and non-AWS clouds (those will be separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for CMK or auto-created KMS key with rotation=true by default
S3 buckets created by module have public access blocked and object-level encryption enforced
Optional immutability mode prevents Terraform from deleting snapshots without explicit approval flag
Snapshot verification job runs automatically after snapshot creation and emits a CloudWatch metric 'StorageSnapshot.Verified' with tags{module_key, env}
A Terraform data source 'storage_snapshot_verification' returns 'OK' or 'FAILED' and can be used in CI to gate upgrades
Comprehensive unit and integration tests in CI (terratest + terraform-compliance) for major code paths
Migration docs with step-by-step upgrade path and canary instructions published to the repo CONVEYOR and linked in the module README
tests: Unit: terraform fmt + validate + tflint rules including custom rules for encryption
Integration: terratest creates resources in a dev account, triggers snapshot + verification job, asserts CloudWatch metric exists
Policy tests: terraform-compliance scenarios for deny-unencrypted and block-public-access
E2E: CI pipeline gate that uses 'storage_snapshot_verification' data source to prevent module version bump if verification FAILED
rollout_plan: 1) Merge as beta behind module flag 'enable_immutability' default=false. 2) Release v2.0.0-beta with README and migration notes. 3) Run canary in staging (private-deploy-staging) for two weeks, monitor 'StorageSnapshot.Verified' and service-level: snapshot restore latency. 4) Toggle default to true in a later release after team signoff and security review. 5) Provide a CLI helper script for operators to migrate existing snapshots to immutability policy.
